samples.summary: The new nesting cap covers every reader and the layout, but not the write boundary that the cap's own rationale names as the untrusted producer (DOCX import / paste → `setDocument` → `writeFullDocument` → recursive `buildBlockNode`)
samples.evidence: `table-nesting.ts` and the `layoutCellBlocks` comment both justify the cap by "the layout takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste), so it bounds itself rather than trusting its input". That input reaches the CRDT through an *un*bounded path: `apply-imported-content.ts:226` / `docs-view.tsx:396` call `store.setDocument(pending)` → `yorkie-doc-store.ts:996 writeFullDocument` → `buildBlockNode` ⇄ `buildCellNode`/`buildRowNode` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:365-412), which recurses once per nesting level with no depth argument and no cap. The same holds for the model-side walks the imported document is then queried with: `Doc.findBlock` → `walkCellsForBlock` (document.ts:75) and `walkCellsForSiblings` (document.ts:97) recurse per nesting level unbounded. Attack: hand a user a .docx (or a clipboard payload) whose tables nest tens of thousands of levels; the importing tab throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` inside the Yorkie `doc.update` callback before any capped reader ever runs. The new `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` is exported from both entry points and could be applied at these sinks; it is not.

samples.summary: The API write boundary accepts table nesting one level deeper than the new reader cap materializes, and its ceiling is a duplicated literal rather than the newly exported constant
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` rejects only `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (controller.ts:443, `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` at controller.ts:806), so a *table* block at depth 32 is accepted and `writeDocsRoot` persists it. The new reader truncates a table at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (crdt-tree.ts:225, frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:480), i.e. a table at depth 32 reads as `rows: []`. An authenticated write-scoped API key can therefore `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content` with content that the server stores in full and that every reader (frontend, engine, backend `readDocsRoot`, revision-history preview) silently drops — an invariant gap between what the store accepts and what readers will ever show. The two ceilings are also independent literals in different packages, so a later bump of one silently re-opens the stack-overflow the other exists to close; the constant is now exported from `@wafflebase/docs` (both `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts`, which the backend already imports from) and could be the single source.

samples.summary: The new shared `resolveCellGesture` calls the throwing `Doc.getBlock`, so a stale or unresolvable table id now aborts the shift+click gesture with an uncaught exception as well as the drag
samples.evidence: `resolveCellGesture` dereferences `this.doc.getBlock(anchorTableId).tableData` (text-editor.ts:3965) and `this.doc.getBlock(resolveTableId).tableData` (3989). `getBlock` throws `Block not found: <id>` when the id resolves through neither the block arrays nor `findBlockInCells` (document.ts:239) — exactly the outcome the new cycle guard in `findBlockInCells` produces for a peer-written parent chain that loops, and the outcome a concurrent remote delete produces for a `blockParentMap` entry left stale since the last layout. The drag path already had this shape, but the shift+click path (text-editor.ts:2093-2095) previously never called `getBlock` with a table id; routing it through the shared resolver widens the crash-on-untrusted-id surface to a second gesture, where the throw escapes the `mousedown` handler and leaves the gesture (and any armed drag state) half-applied. `findBlock` (non-throwing) plus an `undefined` return would match the `undefined`-on-unresolvable contract the rest of this change adopts.

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — buildBlockNode/buildCellNode/buildRowNode (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-414) and writeFullDocument (:3207-3274) carry no depth argument — but the security claim built on it does not hold, and one of the two named producers is already guarded. (a) The paste producer is capped: clipboard.ts:71 defines MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8, enforced at clipboard.ts:308 with depth threaded through sanitizeBlocks/sanitizeBlock/sanitizeCell (:283-412), so no clipboard payload reaches the store past depth 8. (b) For DOCX the store is not the failure point: DocxImporter.convertTable recurses into nested w:tbl at docx-importer.ts:414-415 with no depth argument, so the RangeError fires in the parser (docx-actions.ts:31) before a Document exists to pass to setDocument — a cap at buildBlockNode would not close the stated vector. (c) There is no cross-user or persistence impact: writeFullDocument assembles all children inside a single doc.update before any tree edit, docs-view.tsx:395-407 catches the throw and retains the pending import, and every reader/layout path is capped (crdt-tree.ts:225, yorkie-doc-store.ts:480, table-layout.ts:145), so no depth exists where a writer succeeds and a peer's reader overflows. The residual is a local, fail-closed RangeError in the tab of the user who chose to import the hostile file — an availability/hardening nit, outside the security lane (authz, secrets, injection, crypto/auth, SSRF, deserialization, traversal) and below the blocking bar.

finding.summary: Clamping bounds the rectangle to the table, but the table size is itself peer-chosen and `expandCellRangeForMerges` is an O(area) fixed-point scan run once per paint per peer selection
finding.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` clamps `start`/`end` to the table and then calls `expandCellRangeForMerges(ordered, table)` (line 146), a `while (changed)` loop whose inner `for (r) for (c)` scans the whole rectangle each pass. `normalizeRange` is reached from `computeSelectionRects`, which `editor.ts:2098` calls once per peer per paint (and `getSelectionRects` calls for the local selection). Row count is not banded anywhere — `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (numeric-attrs.ts:95) caps columns at 256 but nothing caps `rows.length` — so a peer who writes a very large table and publishes `tableCellRange` `{start:{0,0}, end:{1e9,1e9}}` gets clamped to the *full table* and then re-scanned each frame, including on paint-only renders where the table layout is not recomputed. `maxCol` additionally reduces over every row on each call. Residual, not introduced: the change also newly routes *nested* tables into this expansion via the `resolveNestedTableLayout` fallback (line 191), widening what reaches it. A cheap fix is to cap the clamped rectangle's area (or the fixed-point pass count) rather than only its indices.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the tree. `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:132-147) clamps only the indices — `maxRow = table.rows.length - 1`, `maxCol` via a per-call reduce over every row — and then unconditionally calls `expandCellRangeForMerges(ordered, table)` at line 146, so a peer-published `tableCellRange` of `{start:{0,0}, end:{1e9,1e9}}` collapses to the FULL table rectangle rather than being rejected. `expandCellRangeForMerges` (selection.ts:56-98) is a `while (changed)` fixed point whose body scans every cell of that rectangle; worse than the reviewer states, line 84-88 invokes `findMergeTopLeft` for each covered cell (`colSpan === 0`), and `findMergeTopLeft` (selection.ts:33-45) scans backward over O(r*c) cells before giving up, making a single pass O(area^2) for a table of covered markers with no spanning parent. Row count is genuinely unbanded: `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256` exists (numeric-attrs.ts:95, enforced at numeric-attrs.ts:256/380 and docs-content.controller.ts:1141) and spans are banded (docs-content.controller.ts:1155-1163), but grep across packages found no cap on `rows.length`. The path is peer-reachable per frame: docs-view.tsx:257 copies `sel.tableCellRange` verbatim from presence into `PeerCursor.selection`, and editor.ts:2098 calls `computeSelectionRects` once per peer per render, gated only by `isRangeVisible(anchor.blockId, focus.blockId)` (editor.ts:2095), which bounds nothing about the rectangle; selection.ts:819 does the same for the local selection. The nested-table fallback at selection.ts:189-191 does newly route nested tables into the same expansion. No guard elsewhere makes it unreachable, so this is a real untrusted-input-driven resource-exhaustion vector that hangs every viewer's tab, the same hazard class the repo's own numeric bands and cycle guards exist to close.

finding.summary: The cycle-guard sweep missed two recursive parent-map walks: `moveToNextCell` / `moveToPrevCell` recurse through `blockParentMap` with no visited set
finding.evidence: This PR adds `seen` guards to six walks over `blockParentMap` on the stated threat model that a peer can write two tables whose ids make the parent chain loop (ids come verbatim from CRDT attributes; the map is built in table-layout.ts:451 keyed on those ids, so duplicate ids across two tables produce A→B and B→A). Two walks over the same map were left unguarded: `moveToNextCell` recurses at text-editor.ts:6007 after moving the caret into the parent cell, and `moveToPrevCell` at text-editor.ts:6065 does the same. With a cyclic map, Tab / Shift+Tab at a table boundary ping-pongs between the two tables until the stack overflows (RangeError out of the key handler) — the same crash the PR closes in `Doc.findBlockInCells`. Confidence is low because the Tab path may pass `addRowAtEnd`, which takes the insert-row branch before the exit branch on the last cell; Shift+Tab (`moveToPrevCell`) has no such branch.

verdict.reason: The two recursive walks exist exactly as described and are unguarded: moveToNextCell reads blockParentMap at text-editor.ts:5992 and self-recurses at :6007; moveToPrevCell reads it at :6052 and self-recurses at :6065, neither carrying a visited set or depth bound. Both are reachable from untrusted-input-driven UI paths: handleTab at :2726-2737 (Shift+Tab -> moveToPrevCell, which has no addRowAtEnd short-circuit) and the arrow-key handlers at :3063/:3088 which call them with addRowAtEnd=false, taking the exit/recursion branch. The cycle threat model is the repository's own, not the reviewer's: identical walks over the same map were given explicit `seen` guards with comments naming peer-written CRDT block ids as the source (findOuterCellAddress text-editor.ts:3894/3902-3906, findOutermostTableId :3919-3924, walkToTopLevelBlockId selection.ts:161-174, Doc.findBlockInCells document.ts:271-290), and selection.ts:111-131 frames the class as "one peer's attribute hangs everyone's tab". The map is keyed verbatim on block ids at table-layout.ts:451 with no uniqueness validation on that path, so a looping parent chain is representable. No caller-side guard intercepts it — isInCell/getCellInfo (:3785-3793) are plain Map.has/Map.get. Unbounded recursion on peer-controlled data crashing the key handler is untrusted-input hardening in the same lane the rest of this change addresses, so none of not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope applies.
